rubric.why: Identifies the temporary nature of the storage.
rubric.description: States that it stores data temporarily.
rubric.how: Award for a clear statement that data is held for a short time or while being processed.

rubric.why: Gives a correct example or explains what happens when temporary storage loses power.
rubric.description: Names RAM as an example, or states that its contents are lost when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Award for RAM or the loss of stored data when power is off.

modelAnswer: Temporary storage holds data and instructions for a short time while the computer is processing them.
RAM is an example; its contents are lost when the power is switched off.

rubric.why: Identifies that software is copied or used without permission.
rubric.description: States that software is copied or used without authorization.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning unauthorized or illegal copying or use.

rubric.why: Clarifies that the software is protected or used without a valid license or permission.
rubric.description: Identifies the protected software or lack of license or permission.
rubric.how: Award for a reference to copyrighted software, lack of a license, or lack of permission.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying, distribution, or use of copyrighted software.
It violates the software owner's rights and the terms of its license.

rubric.why: Identifies the act involved in softlifting.
rubric.description: States that a software copy is installed, copied, or shared.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the act of making or using an additional software copy.

rubric.why: Explains that the copy exceeds the license terms or is shared without permission.
rubric.description: States that the software is used on more computers than the license allows or is shared without authorization.
rubric.how: Award for an explicit reference to exceeding the license or unauthorized sharing.

modelAnswer: Softlifting is copying or installing software on more computers than the license permits.
It can also include sharing a licensed copy with others without permission.

items.followUp: Explain software sharing with an example.

rubric.why: Describes hardware sharing as making hardware resources available to multiple computers.
rubric.description: States that computers share hardware resources or devices.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that multiple computers can use the same hardware.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of a shared hardware device.
rubric.description: Gives a printer shared by computers as an example.
rubric.how: Award for a clear printer-sharing example.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing means allowing several computers to use the same hardware device or resource.
For example, computers on a network can share one printer.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a private IP address and a public IP address?

rubric.why: Gives the defining feature of a static IP address.
rubric.description: States that a static IP address is fixed or does not change.
rubric.how: Award for a correct description of its stable assignment.

rubric.why: Gives the defining feature of a dynamic IP address.
rubric.description: States that a dynamic IP address is assigned automatically and can change.
rubric.how: Award for automatic assignment or the possibility of change.

modelAnswer: A static IP address is fixed and normally remains the same.
A dynamic IP address is assigned automatically, usually by DHCP, and may change.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of HTTPS?

rubric.why: Identifies HTTP as the protocol used for web communication.
rubric.description: Names HTTP or identifies it as a web communication protocol.

rubric.why: Explains what HTTP is used to transfer and between which systems.
rubric.description: States that HTTP transfers web pages or content between a web server and a browser.
rubric.how: Award for a correct web-content transfer use.

modelAnswer: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer web pages and other web content.
It enables communication between a web browser and a web server.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a bus topology and a star topology.

rubric.why: Identifies the direct, dedicated connection in point-to-point communication.
rubric.description: States that a point-to-point connection links two devices directly, usually over a dedicated link.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning two devices or a dedicated direct link.

rubric.why: Identifies that a multipoint connection is shared by multiple devices.
rubric.description: States that a multipoint connection allows more than two devices to share a link or channel.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning multiple devices sharing a connection.

modelAnswer: A point-to-point connection provides a dedicated link between two devices.
A multipoint connection allows more than two devices to share a single link or channel.

items.followUp: What is an unordered list in HTML?

rubric.why: Explains that an ordered list displays items in a defined sequence.
rubric.description: States that an ordered list presents items in sequence, usually numbered or lettered.
rubric.how: Award for describing the ordered sequence or numbering of its items.

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML tag or a typical marker used for an ordered list.
rubric.description: Names the <ol> tag or indicates that items are marked with numbers or letters.
rubric.how: Award for a correct tag or numbering/lettering detail.

modelAnswer: An ordered list is an HTML list whose items are displayed in a specific sequence, usually with numbers or letters.
It is created with the <ol> tag, with each item placed inside an <li> tag.
